My family has farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. I know this soil. At 69, I am not going to try something new — my knees hurt and my son lives in the city now. I do what I know: winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields, same as every year. This rotation is what the land here is suited for, and I can manage it without reading anything or hiring much help except at harvest and planting when I rent the village machine.

I have about 6 mu. All of it goes to wheat then corn — no point dividing it up for vegetables or peanuts, I don't have the energy to tend them and the market is uncertain. I'll buy wheat seed from the cooperative — the improved variety they've been pushing for a few years now gives good yield. For corn I always use hybrid seed, everyone does, the yield is much better than the old kinds.

For fertilizer I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then add urea when the crop is putting on growth. I learned from watching and doing, not from any school. I water wheat three times — before winter sets in, when it joints, and when it heads. Corn usually gets rain in summer so once is enough if the rains come. If July is dry I water again.

I'll plough before wheat to turn the soil properly. After wheat I use the rotary tiller — faster and I can hire it cheaply. Pesticides I apply twice on wheat for weeds and disease in spring, once on corn for pests.
